mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during early-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during late-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate a strong demand for goods and services, leading to increased economic growth, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in the supply of goods and services, leading to decreased prices, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during early-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending, which in turn drives up the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during late-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index indicates decreased demand for goods and services, leading to decreased economic growth, which in turn drives down the S&P 500 over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
